correctness.rationale: The explicitly constructed period propagator is (P exp(T A1/2))^2 and is strictly positive for m,T>0. Its positive eigenvalue gives the arsinh formula. The strictly convex auxiliary F proves positive T derivative; an exact positive square comparison proves positive m derivative; the implicit function theorem gives a unique strictly decreasing zero frontier. The low-migration exponent and high-migration x coth x limit follow from the exact zero equation and uniqueness. 128 independent matrix exponential comparisons and an exact a=1,b=3,m=2 threshold verify computations without replacing the infinite-parameter proof.

value.rationale: The source explicitly asks for asymptotic form of the critical migration-period curve in its directed-season model. The theorem solves that natural quantitative persistence gap for equal seasonal habitat rates with a global closed formula, sharp logarithmic and inverse-rate critical laws, and unique cutoff for any positive migration. These facts can benchmark ecological seasonal tracking and distinguish rigorous cutoff geometry from numerical diagrams, without claiming general networks or nonlinear stochastic survival.
